**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 81, verses 15–29**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Al-khunas* (the ones that recede): those that withdraw by day, meaning they become hidden and appear again by night.

*Al-jawari al-kunas* (the ones that run and hide): those that run at times and at other times hide in their *makanis* (lairs). The *makanis* are their places of shelter, like the lairs of wild oxen. They are the five planets: Utarid (Mercury), Zuhara (Venus), Mirrikh (Mars), Mushtari (Jupiter), and Zuhal (Saturn).

*Idha 'as'asa* (when it approaches or departs): meaning it draws near or turns away, because *'as'asa* is one of the words with opposite meanings (*asmaa' al-adhdad*).

*Tanaffasa* (breathed): meaning it extended until it became clear daylight.

*Innahu* (indeed it): meaning the Qur'an.

*Li-qawli rasulin karim* (the word of a noble messenger): meaning Jibril, noble before Allah, and the Qur'an is attributed to him because he brought it down.

*Dhu quwwah* (possessing power): meaning of great strength.

*'Inda dhi al-'arshi makin* (established in the presence of the Lord of the Throne): meaning he has a high rank with Allah, the Exalted.

*Muta' thumma amin* (obeyed, then trustworthy): meaning he is obeyed in the heavens, the angels obey him, and he is trustworthy with the revelation.

*Wa ma sahibukum bi-majnun* (your companion is not mad): meaning Muhammad (ﷺ) is not affected by madness.

*Wa laqad ra'ahu bi-al-ufuq al-mubin* (he certainly saw him on the clear horizon): meaning the Prophet (ﷺ) saw Jibril in his true form, the form in which he was created, on the high, clear horizon on the eastern side.

*Wa ma huwa 'ala al-ghayb* (and he is not withholding the unseen): meaning Muhammad (ﷺ) does not withhold the unseen, which is what is hidden of revelation and the news of the heavens.

*Bi-dannin* (stingy): meaning not miserly. In another reading it is read with the letter *zay* (*bi-zanin*), meaning accused, so that he would be suspected of reducing it and not giving all of it.

*Wa ma huwa bi-qawli shaytanin rajim* (and it is not the word of an accursed devil): meaning the Qur'an is not the speech of a devil who eavesdrops and is stoned.

*Fa-ayna tadhhabun* (where then are you going?): meaning which path will you take in denying the Qur'an and turning away from it?

*In huwa illa dhikrun li-al-'alamin* (it is only a reminder to the worlds): meaning the Qur'an is only an admonition to humans and jinn.

*An yastaqim* (to be upright): meaning to seek the truth, believe in it, and act in accordance with it.

*Wa ma tasha'una illa an yasha'a Allah* (and you will not will except that Allah wills): meaning whoever among you wills uprightness, he has only willed it after Allah had willed it for him beforehand, for if Allah had not willed it, His servant would not have willed it.

**The meaning of the verses:**

When Allah, the Exalted, established the belief in resurrection and recompense with a complete description of its events, and since this description came through revelation, the subject required the soundness of revelation and belief in it. If revelation is sound and the servant believes in it, he believes in the soundness of resurrection and recompense. Hence Allah, the Exalted, swore by the greatest oath that the Qur'an was brought down by Jibril to Muhammad (ﷺ), and that what Muhammad (ﷺ) says is the speech of Allah and His revelation. He is not mad, saying what he does not know and babbling about what has no meaning, nor is he the speech of an accursed devil from among those who eavesdrop and convey it to their companions among the soothsayers. Rather, it is the speech of Allah, true and genuine, and what it informs of is true as it informs. So Allah said, ﴿Nay﴾, meaning the matter is not as you claim, that what our Messenger says is of the same kind as what soothsayers say. Nor is it of the kind that poets say, nor is it the speech of madmen, nor is it the magic of magicians. He swore by ﴿the stars that recede, that run and hide﴾, meaning by everything that recedes, runs, and hides, such as gazelles, wild oxen, the stars, and the five planets: Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn.

By *khunus* is meant disappearance, and by *kunus* is meant their retreat to their *makanis*, their places of shelter. His saying, ﴿and by the night when it approaches﴾, meaning He swore by the night when it draws near or turns away, since the word *'as'asa* means both approached and departed, so it is a word shared between approach and departure. ﴿And by the morning when it breathes﴾, meaning when its light has extended and it has become clear daylight. He swore by all these things that the Qur'an, which describes for you resurrection and recompense in the truest description, is ﴿the word of a noble messenger﴾, meaning Jibril, noble before his Lord, ﴿possessing power﴾ whose power cannot be measured, so neither humans nor jinn can snatch what he has of revelation, nor add to it or subtract from it. ﴿Established in the presence of the Lord of the Throne﴾, the Glorified and Exalted, meaning of honored rank, ﴿obeyed in the heavens, trustworthy with the revelation﴾. This is the first point. The second is that ﴿your companion Muhammad (ﷺ) is not mad﴾ as you claim, ﴿and he certainly saw him﴾, meaning the Prophet (ﷺ) saw Jibril ﴿on the clear horizon﴾, he saw him in the form in which Allah created him, and he has six hundred wings. He saw him on the horizon on the eastern side, and he filled the whole horizon, and the horizon was clear and the day was rising. ﴿And he is not﴾, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿withholding the unseen﴾, meaning he is not one suspected of adding to it, subtracting from it, altering it, or changing it, but conveys it as it is. He is not stingy, so that one might suspect him of concealing anything or hiding it out of miserliness, or of reducing it out of greed and avarice. ﴿And it is not the word of an accursed devil﴾ from among those who eavesdrop and pass it to their human allies, mixing into it and lying.

His saying, ﴿Where then are you going?﴾, rebukes them for their shameful course in denying His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), accusing him of magic, and describing the Qur'an as poetry, soothsaying, and fables. His saying, ﴿It is only a reminder to the worlds﴾, meaning the noble Qur'an is only a reminder to the worlds of humans and jinn, by which they remember their Creator, their Provider, the One who gives them life and causes them to die, and the right to worship and the duty of gratitude He is owed. They are admonished by it, so they fear their Lord, and do not disobey Him by abandoning the duties He imposed on them or by committing what He forbade them. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿for whoever among you wills to be upright﴾, meaning to follow the path of truth: first by seeking the truth, second by believing in it and acting in accordance with it.

When Abu Jahl heard this verse, ﴿for whoever among you wills to be upright﴾, he said: "The matter is up to us. If we will, we become upright, and if we will not, we do not." Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed, ﴿And you will not will except that Allah, Lord of the worlds, wills﴾. So the accursed one was humbled. Know that whoever among the worlds wills uprightness has only willed it after Allah, the Exalted, had willed it for him. And if Allah, the Exalted, had not willed it, the servant would never have willed it, since the will of Allah precedes the will of the servant. In everything a person wills, the will of Allah precedes his will, because the human is a servant, Allah is the Lord, and no will precedes the will of the Lord.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. The permissibility of swearing by Allah, the Exalted, and by His names and attributes.
2. The affirmation of revelation and the establishment of Muhammad's prophethood (ﷺ).
3. The explanation of Jibril's perfect qualities: trustworthiness, strength, high rank, obedience, and nobility.
4. The exoneration of the Messenger from what the polytheists accused him of.
5. The explanation that the will of Allah precedes the will of the servant, so nothing occurs in Allah's dominion except what He wills.
